cases.question: What is the current evidence for GLP-1 receptor agonists in obesity treatment?
cases.reference_answer: GLP-1-based medications and multiagonists can achieve up to 24% weight loss in the management of obesity. GLP-1 agonists affect diverse obesity etiopathogenic processes including food intake regulation, insulin resistance, and inflammation. GLP-1RAs significantly reduce total body weight, fat mass, and lean mass in adults with diabetes, overweight, or obesity. Tirzepatide and semaglutide are among the most effective for weight and fat mass reduction but are associated with significant lean mass reduction. Activation of the GLP-1 receptor helps reduce body weight by promoting satiety and delaying gastric emptying.

reference_context.excerpt: Thanks to biochemical engineering, the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) molecule has emerged as an essential element in the development of diverse agonists and multiagonists, based in the GLP-1 structure for obesity treatment. These new antiobesity medications can reach up to 24% weight loss, which makes possible an effective management of obesity and its complications.

reference_context.title: Effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and co-agonists on body composition: Systematic review and network meta-analysis.
reference_context.excerpt: This meta-analysis evaluated the effects of GLP-1RAs and GLP-1/GIP receptor dual agonists (GLP-1/GIP-RAs) on body composition, focusing on total weight, fat mass, and lean mass in adults with diabetes and/or overweight/obesity. GLP-1RAs significantly reduced total body weight (MD -3.55 kg, 95 %-CI [-4.81, -2.29]), fat mass (MD -2.95 kg, 95 %-CI [-4.11, -1.79]), and lean mass (MD -0.86 kg, 95 %-CI [-1.30, -0.42]), with lean mass loss comprising approximately 25 % of the total weight loss.

reference_context.title: Effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and co-agonists on body composition: Systematic review and network meta-analysis.
reference_context.excerpt: Tirzepatide (15 mg weekly) and semaglutide (2.4 mg weekly) were the most effective for weight and fat mass reduction but were among the least effective in preserving lean mass. CONCLUSIONS: Potent GLP-1 RAs, such as tirzepatide and semaglutide, demonstrate greater overall weight loss but are associated with a significant reduction in lean mass.

reference_context.title: Obesity and GLP-1.
reference_context.excerpt: Through activation of the GLP-1 receptor they not only have an important role stimulating insulin secretion after meals, but with their extrapancreatic actions, both peripheral and central, they also help reduce body weight by promoting satiety and delaying gastric emptying. Liraglutide in a dose of 3 mg is currently the only drug of this group that is approved by the FDA to treat obesity, with weight losses up to 8.5 kg in relatively short periods of time.

cases.question: What are the demonstrated clinical successes and current challenges of CAR-T cell therapy in hematologic versus solid tumors?
cases.reference_answer: CAR-T cell therapy has demonstrated clinical success in hematologic malignancies. The efficacy of CAR-T cell therapy in solid tumors is limited by antigenic heterogeneity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Research efforts aim to improve solid-tumor CAR-T therapy by enhancing T-cell persistence, targeting multiple antigens, and employing allogeneic manufacturing approaches. Key challenges for CAR-T therapy in solid tumors include antigen selection, tolerability, and safety concerns. CAR-T therapy is expected to become an important component of individualized cancer immunotherapy in the future.

cases.question: What are current approaches and computational strategies being explored for quantum error correction using rotated surface codes?
cases.reference_answer: Hierarchical QEC schemes concatenate hypergraph product codes with rotated surface codes of distance 5 to enable hardware compatibility through lattice surgery. Adaptive confidence-gated neural decoding frameworks for the rotated surface code route low-confidence predictions to a minimum-weight perfect matching refinement stage. The Sparse Mamba Decoder processes only active detection events with O(k) complexity using a Mamba state-space backbone for efficient surface code syndrome processing. Simulations of rotated surface codes with code distance 5 evaluate logical error probabilities under realistic noise models incorporating both stochastic Pauli and coherent errors.

reference_context.title: Hierarchical Quantum Error Correction with Hypergraph Product Code and Rotated Surface Code
reference_context.excerpt: We propose and analyze a hierarchical quantum error correction (QEC) scheme that concatenates hypergraph product (HGP) codes with rotated surface codes and that is compatible with quantum computers with only nearest-neighbor interactions. The outer code employs (3,4)-random HGP codes, known for their constant encoding rate and favorable distance scaling, while the inner code consists of a rotated surface code with distance 5, allowing hardware compatibility through lattice surgery.

reference_context.title: Latency-Constrained Hardware-Aware Quantum Error Correction Co-Design with Adaptive Confidence-Gated Neural Decoding for the Rotated Surface Code
reference_context.excerpt: We present an adaptive confidence-gated decoding framework for the rotated surface code that treats decoding as a two-stage inference problem. A lightweight feed-forward neural network performs fast-path decoding for the majority of syndrome measurements, while only low-confidence predictions are escalated to a minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) refinement stage.

reference_context.title: Sparse Mamba Decoder for Quantum Error Correction: Efficient Defect-Centric Processing of Surface Code Syndromes
reference_context.excerpt: At physically relevant error rates (p ~ 0.1%), fewer than 5% of syndrome entries contain active detection events -- yet existing decoders process the entire syndrome volume. We introduce the Sparse Mamba Decoder (SMD), a defect-centric neural decoder that processes only the k active detection events using a 13-dimensional feature representation per defect and a Mamba state-space backbone, achieving $O(k)$ complexity.

reference_context.title: Simulation and performance analysis of quantum error correction with a rotated surface code under a realistic noise model
reference_context.excerpt: In this work, we performed a full simulation of QEC for the rotated surface codes with a code distance 5, which employs 49 qubits and is within reach of the current state-of-the-art quantum computers. In particular, we evaluate the logical error probability in a realistic noise model that incorporates not only stochastic Pauli errors but also coherent errors due to a systematic control error or unintended interactions.

One approach concatenates hypergraph product codes with rotated surface codes using lattice surgery, employing soft-decision decoding with belief propagation and ordered statistics decoding. cases.question: How are diffusion models used for image generation, and what are their limitations?
cases.reference_answer: Diffusion models have revolutionized the visual generation landscape with impressive text-guided generative functions. Diffusion models are utilized for text-to-image generation, text-guided image editing, and conditional generation with specific or multiple conditions. Relying solely on text conditioning does not fully cater to the varied and complex requirements of different applications. Transformer-based diffusion models face a trade-off between visual fidelity and computational complexity due to the quadratic nature of self-attention operations. Larger patch sizes in Transformer-based diffusion models struggle to capture fine-grained visual details, leading to image distortions.

cases.question: What are the opportunities and risks associated with artificial intelligence in drug discovery and antibody development?
cases.reference_answer: AI methods can revolutionize drug discovery by reducing the time and cost required for drug development and generating de novo binders for target antigens. Artificial intelligence shifts development processes from empirical trial-and-error to data-driven engineering by integrating sequence, structural, and molecular dynamics features. Despite advancements, limitations of AI-based methods must still be addressed for effective incorporation into therapeutic and diagnostic applications. Progress in targeted treatments like antibody-drug conjugates is constrained by the combinatorial complexity of design, toxicity and side effects, and variable clinical benefit. Deep learning models often remain elusive to interpretation by the human mind, creating a demand for explainable artificial intelligence.

reference_context.excerpt: In this paper, we argue that FMs are catalyzing a transition toward a new scientific paradigm. cases.question: According to recent genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screens, which genetic factors have been identified as regulators of T-cell exhaustion or fitness, and how does their perturbation affect T-cell persistence or antitumor activity?
cases.reference_answer: Epigenetic factors, including INO80 and BAF chromatin-remodeling complexes, were identified as regulators of T-cell exhaustion by genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screens. Depletion of the BAF complex subunit Arid1a maintains an effector program, down-regulates exhaustion-related genes, limits exhaustion-associated chromatin accessibility, and improves antitumor immunity. Inactivation of Ctbp1 enhances functional T-cell persistence specifically under chronic stimulation conditions. Ablation of Dap5 increases translation and enhances tumor-killing across intense, acute, and chronic stimulation modes. Loss of Icam1-mediated homotypic T-cell clustering amplifies expansion and effector functions after acute and intense stimulation.

cases.question: How do linear attention and state-space models improve efficiency on long-context sequence modeling compared to traditional architectures?
cases.reference_answer: Transformer architectures have time complexity that scales quadratically with sequence length. State-space models offer alternative sub-quadratic solutions and linear-time recurrence with linear O(N) computational complexity. Linear attention and state space models have become popular for improving long-context efficiency in large language models. Systems like StateFlow partition sequences to reduce activation lifetimes and improve training throughput for models with linear recurrence.

reference_context.title: StateFlow: Sequence Pipeline Parallelism for Long-Context Modeling with Linear Recurrence
reference_context.excerpt: Long-context training is increasingly important for large language models, and linear attention and state space models have become popular for improving long-context efficiency. StateFlow further uses profile-guided nonuniform chunking to balance recurrence and softmax attention computation in hybrid models, and overlaps state transitions that expose limited parallelism with surrounding computation.

reference_context.title: StateFlow: Sequence Pipeline Parallelism for Long-Context Modeling with Linear Recurrence
reference_context.excerpt: We present StateFlow, a sequence pipeline parallelism system for models with linear recurrence. StateFlow partitions each sequence into chunks and schedules their execution while propagating boundary states and gradients across chunks, thereby reducing activation lifetimes and improving training throughput.
